key_insight: MedKIT shows that models can memorize updated medical facts without reliably using them across new wording, reasoning, or real task settings.
clinical_relevance: In medicine, where evidence changes quickly, this gap means updated LLM knowledge may still be unsafe or unhelpful unless it generalizes beyond simple recall.
method: Built MedKIT, a benchmark for medical knowledge updates and transfer.
Tested transfer across lexical variation, relational changes, compositional reasoning, and open-ended operationalization.
Included locality checks to see whether updating one fact harms other knowledge.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluated 12 knowledge-integration strategies across 5 models and found strong gains on recall and lexical variation, but little to no improvement on compositional or operational tasks.
watch_item: These results come from benchmark probes, so real-world clinical performance may differ and should not be assumed from recall improvements alone.
paper_title: MedKIT: Evaluating Knowledge Integration and Generalization in Large Language Models
